newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd's chairman says committed to broker system.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's chairman says committed to broker system.

text.p: Lloyd's of London chairman Sir David Rowland said in a speech due to be delivered in New York later on Thursday that the insurance market would work with insurance brokers to make distribution more cost effective.

"Lloyd's is fully committed to the broker distribution channel and we are keen to work with brokers to enhance the cost effectiveness of distribution -- not to pare profit margins that are under enough pressure already, but to exploit our skills and technology to reduce transmission costs," Rowland said.

Brokers and underwriters were both under pressure to reduce transmission costs and it was no coincidence that high transaction costs have been accompanied by the increasing popularity of alternative sources of insurance, he added.

Rowland, in New York to receive an award from the city's College of Insurance for being insurance leader of the year, said it was "only by making our clients understand the efficiency with which we deliver our products that we can maximise our business opportunities".
Lloyd's, Rowland said, would concentrate on key issues facing the industry, including "how to bring the benefits of high quality and security efficiently and economically" to clients.
